pull.title: MINOR: Skip further reads from log for share fetches if max records reached
pull.body:
On the slow path, `DelayedShareFetch.combineLogReadResponse` reuses the
data read in `tryComplete` and issues a second `readFromLog` for
partitions that became acquirable only at completion. The second read
was issued even when the already fetched data covered `maxFetchRecords`,
in which case `SharePartition.acquire` receives a zero budget and
returns empty, so the read was wasted.

The remaining record budget is now computed from the already fetched
data and the second read is skipped when nothing remains. Skipped
partitions are absent from the response, as share sessions already do
for partitions without data, and their locks are released on the same
path as before.

Reviewers: Abhinav Dixit <adixit@confluent.io>, Andrew Schofield
 <aschofield@confluent.io>

repo.name: kafka
repo.description: Apache Kafka - A distributed event streaming platform

reviews.body: Thanks for the PR. Mostly looks good to me. One question

Thanks for the PR. An AI-assisted review suggests this PR is a regression in behaviour.

The skip drops the partitions that currently have first claim on the budget (DelayedShareFetch.java:849). The new comment says "the already fetched records are handed out first". They are not. The merge at the end of `combineLogReadResponse` does `missingTopicPartitionsLogReadResponse.putAll(existingFetchedData)`, so the missing partitions sit first in the combined map, and processFetchResponse acquires in map order with `maxFetchRecords - acquiredRecordsCount`. So before this change the missing partitions were acquired first and the already-fetched ones got the remainder. After it, the already-fetched span is used to decide the missing ones get nothing. Concrete scenario, one consumer, tp0 and tp1 both with deep backlogs:
- tp0 is served, so its next fetch offset moves and its cached fetch-offset metadata goes stale. It is read in tryComplete and lands in the already-fetched set every time.
- tp1 is not served, so its offset and cached metadata stay valid. It is never read in tryComplete and is always a "missing" partition.
- Before the change, tp1 was acquired first on each fetch and the two alternated naturally. After it, tp0's span is at least maxFetchRecords, so tp1 is skipped on every fetch for as long as tp0 has a backlog. That is indefinite starvation of tp1.

review_comments.body: what is the case when startOffset is not found in `fetchOffsets`?

review_comments.diff_hunk:
@@ -840,6 +842,14 @@ CompletableFuture<LinkedHashMap<TopicIdPartition, LogReadResult>> combineLogRead
             return CompletableFuture.completedFuture(existingFetchedData);
         }
 
+        // The already fetched records are handed out first, so only the remainder of the record budget
+        // is available to the missing partitions. If nothing remains then nothing from them could be
+        // acquired, so skip the read altogether; the partitions are simply absent from the response and
+        // their locks are released along with the rest of the acquired partitions.
review_comments.body: The code actually does opposite of the comment. It puts missing first and then the existing ones

review_comments.body: The comment was misleading, I have removed it and wrote a simpler version.
This is just defensive code, ideally fetchOffset should not be empty and in case it is then it anyways gets reset while comparing against baseOffset.
okay, I was thinking maybe if such scenario arrives, we should put a WARNING log and return, but if you think that this is fine, we can go ahead with this way as well

> The skip drops the partitions that currently have first claim on the budget (DelayedShareFetch.java:849). The new comment says "the already fetched records are handed out first". They are not. The merge at the end of `combineLogReadResponse` does `missingTopicPartitionsLogReadResponse.putAll(existingFetchedData)`, so the missing partitions sit first in the combined map, and processFetchResponse acquires in map order with `maxFetchRecords - acquiredRecordsCount`. So before this change the missing partitions were acquired first and the already-fetched ones got the remainder. After it, the already-fetched span is used to decide the missing ones get nothing. Concrete scenario, one consumer, tp0 and tp1 both with deep backlogs:
> 
> * tp0 is served, so its next fetch offset moves and its cached fetch-offset metadata goes stale. It is read in tryComplete and lands in the already-fetched set every time.
> * tp1 is not served, so its offset and cached metadata stay valid. It is never read in tryComplete and is always a "missing" partition.

Yes it's correct that unfortunately that used to happen. But it was not intended, correct me if I am wrong @adixitconfluent. We make best effort basis to acquire and process the partitions in order of partitions in the request. This additional case shall trigger when some partitions are fetched but yet some additional are needed later. However all topics are already acquired. The order is anyways not maintained in this latter case so this change should ideally not cause regression.

Prior calling the delayedsharefetch, partitions are always rotated in share partition manager to prevent starvation.

I (claude) wrote a test and can see starvation of 1 partition. When all fetched records are not sent to client then fetchOffsetMetadata is also bumped for trimmed partitions which extrensically adds the partitions to the missing list. @AndrewJSchofield @adixitconfluent Let me know the choice, I can address that in the `same PR` or `separate PR` or `prior to current PR` (my preference).

Yes, while writing the code for `combineLogReadResponse`, I did not really consider starvation but the sequence of operations ensured that there is no starvation and hence we never faced a problem. I think we should fix the problem  when all the fetched records are not sent to client then we shouldn't update `fetchOffsetMetadata` for the unsent partitions. I am okay if that is in a separate PR or if you want me to take it up.
@apoorvmittal10 I think the starvation needs to be solved, either in this PR or a PR which goes before this one.
